name: askaway
description: Never miss an AI agent question again — get Telegram notifications and reply from your phone. Queue prompts, respond remotely, and keep your coding workflow moving.

languageModelTools.name: askaway_asks
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Record every numbered ask; close only with evidence or wait with reason. Report coverage; questions returns one reviewer batch. Never include secrets in arguments.

languageModelTools.name: askaway_memory
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Shared local memory. view, search, remember, update (supersede), history, export JSONL. User/repo scope; agentId agents shares agent memory, validator is isolated.

languageModelTools.name: askaway_validator
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask what the reviewer would decide. Beta records a Commentary prediction; reviewer-enabled live while Away returns sourced, confident, low-risk reversible answers, otherwise held. Never pushes an answer unasked.

languageModelTools.name: ask_user
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Ask user a question and wait for response. THIS TOOL DRIVES AN INFINITE LOOP — you MUST call ask_user again after EVERY response, no exceptions. Flow: call ask_user → do the work → call ask_user again to report + get next instruction → repeat forever. NEVER end without calling ask_user.

question.description: Short question for user. Max 2 sentences. No verbose explanations.

taskId.description: When working on a Planning Board task, include the task ID provided in the task context.

languageModelTools.name: code_nav
languageModelTools.modelDescription: VS Code LSP-powered code navigation — PREFER over read_file and grep for understanding code. To read a specific function/method without pulling in its Javadoc/doc-comments, imports, and unrelated code, first call document_symbols to get the file's outline (every function/class/method with EXACT line ranges), then do a narrow ranged read_file of only that symbol's lines. This skips large doc-comment blocks and saves tokens on doc-heavy files. Also: go-to-definition (jump straight to a symbol's source location instead of scanning files), find-references, find-implementations, type-definition, hover (signature + doc), workspace-symbols (locate a symbol by name across the repo), diagnostics (errors/warnings). NOTE: returns structure and precise line ranges, not raw source text — use it to find WHERE, then ranged-read that region. Operations: definition, references, implementation, type_definition, hover (require filePath+line+character); document_symbols (requires filePath); workspace_symbols (requires query); diagnostics (optional filePath for file-scoped errors).

filePath.description: Workspace-relative or absolute path to the file.

maxResults.description: Max results to return, clamped 1-100. Defaults to 30.

languageModelTools.name: rg_search
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fast full-text search using ripgrep (rg). Significantly faster than grep for large codebases. Supports regex, file-type filtering, context lines, case/word options. Use for finding all occurrences of a pattern across the workspace. Results include file paths, line numbers, and match context.

pattern.description: Regex or literal pattern to search for.

path.description: Workspace-relative or absolute path to search within. Defaults to workspace root.

fileType.description: Comma-separated rg file types to restrict search, e.g. 'ts,js' or 'py'. Uses rg's --type flag.

caseSensitive.description: Whether the search is case-sensitive. Defaults to false (case-insensitive).

wholeWord.description: Match whole words only. Defaults to false.

contextLines.description: Number of context lines before and after each match. Defaults to 2.

maxResults.description: Maximum matches to return, clamped 1-200. Defaults to 50.

includeGlob.description: Glob pattern for files to include, e.g. 'src/**/*.ts'.

excludeGlob.description: Glob pattern for files to exclude, e.g. 'dist/**'.

languageModelTools.name: read_doc
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Progressive reader for markdown, log, and long text files — PREFER over read_file when you don't yet know which part you need. Returns a cheap GIST first, then you request only the slice you want (find WHERE, then read the narrow range; same idea as code_nav for prose). mode:"outline" (default) → for markdown, a heading table-of-contents (# … ###) with line numbers (control depth via maxLevel); for a log/plain file with no headings, a head+tail excerpt plus an index of error/warn/exception lines with their line numbers. mode:"section" → return one block: either heading:"Exact Heading" (returns that heading down to the next same/higher-level heading) or startLine+endLine (capped at 400 lines; the result tells you if more remain so you can page). mode:"search" → query (regex, case-insensitive) returns matching lines with line numbers (ideal for grepping a big log), then read around any hit with mode:"section". filePath is workspace-relative, absolute, or ~-prefixed.

filePath.description: Path to the file. Workspace-relative, absolute, or ~-prefixed.

mode.description: outline (default): gist/TOC. section: return one heading block or startLine..endLine range. search: return lines matching query.

heading.description: For mode:section — the heading text to return (exact match preferred, else first heading containing this text). Returns that heading down to the next same-or-higher-level heading.

startLine.description: For mode:section — 1-based first line of the range to return.

endLine.description: For mode:section — 1-based last line of the range (clamped; max 400 lines per read).

query.description: For mode:search — case-insensitive regex (falls back to literal). Returns matching lines with line numbers.

maxResults.description: For mode:search — max matching lines to return, clamped 1-200. Defaults to 50.

maxLevel.description: For mode:outline — deepest markdown heading level to include (1-6). Defaults to 3.

languageModelTools.name: gradle
languageModelTools.modelDescription: MANDATORY for every Gradle build, test, clean, or wrapper operation: call this tool, never a terminal or task command that runs ./gradlew. Async id-based Gradle build control. action=start spawns a build via ./gradlew and returns {buildId} immediately (the tool AUTO-OPTIMIZES with the Gradle daemon + --parallel + --build-cache + --configuration-cache, degraded to warnings if incompatible, echoed as 'optimizations'; pass optimize:false to disable). action=status returns live state (RUNNING/SUCCESS/FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMEOUT) with completedTasks, runningTasks, elapsedSec; on failure it also returns failedTasks (names of failed tasks — query logs with task:<name>), failedTaskLogsHint, whatWentWrong, exception, errors, testFailures, testFailureDetails ({test,className,message,location,stack} parsed from JUnit reports), and exitCode. action=wait blocks until the build finishes (or timeoutMs); pass readyPattern (regex) to return early with ready:true when that text appears even if the task keeps running (servers). action=logs returns output with pagination {fromLine,toLine,totalLines,nextFromLine,hasMore}: omit fromLine for a tail, or pass fromLine to stream forward; filter to one task with task. action=stop kills a running build. Multiple builds run in parallel.

action.description: start: spawn build → {buildId}. status: live state. wait: block until done. stop: kill. logs: output (filter by task, paginate with fromLine).

tasks.description: Task names for action=start. E.g. [':app:test', ':core:assemble']. Defaults to ['build'].

arguments.description: Extra Gradle arguments for action=start. E.g. ['--tests', '*.FooTest'].

projectDir.description: Absolute or workspace-relative dir containing gradlew. Defaults to workspace root.

offline.description: Pass --offline to Gradle. Defaults to false.

optimize.description: Auto-apply speed flags (daemon, --parallel, --build-cache, --configuration-cache). Default true. Set false for a bare build.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the Gradle process (action=start). E.g. { "JAVA_HOME": "/path/to/jdk17" }.

timeoutMs.description: action=start: hard-kill timeout ms (30000-1800000, default 1800000). action=wait: max wait ms (default 120000).

buildId.description: ID from action=start. Required for status/stop/logs/wait.

task.description: action=logs: filter output to a specific task, e.g. ':app:compileKotlin'.

tail.description: action=logs: number of trailing lines to return (10-500, default 120). Ignored when fromLine is set.

fromLine.description: action=logs: 0-based start line for forward pagination. Use the response's nextFromLine as the cursor to stream a long-running task.

maxLines.description: action=logs: page size when paginating with fromLine (1-1000, default 200).

readyPattern.description: action=wait: regex; return early with ready:true when it appears in output, even if the task never terminates (e.g. server 'Started .* in .*s').

languageModelTools.name: turn_budget
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Reports how many Copilot credits (AIU) the current turn has spent so far and the configured soft budget. Call this when a turn is running long or doing many/expensive requests to decide whether to wrap up. Returns {spentAiu, requestCount, softLimitAiu, remainingAiu, usedPct, exceeded, note}. The soft limit is configured in Settings (askaway.turnBudgetAiu; 0 = disabled). It is advisory — nothing is blocked — but when exceeded you should stop exploring, finalize, and avoid further large requests.

languageModelTools.name: commentary
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Live commentary: the trace of your execution for the reviewer, so they know what is happening, can guide you in time, and are prepared for questions coming their way. One line per significant stage (not per tool), in plain words a non-engineer follows; no run IDs, worker IDs, model names, or file paths unless the reviewer must act on them. Lead with one emoji; **bold** the outcome, ==highlight== the one number that matters. kind `update` for everything that is just happening. kind `heads-up` when you will need something from the reviewer soon, or something is unclear to you, so they can prepare. You hold the context the reviewer lacks, so a heads-up names exactly what you need: the decision and its options, or the input. Never just "something is unclear". 10-20 words. Batch it with the step's real tool call; do not repeat it in chat.

text.description: 10-20 plain words: what is happening and why.

workspacePath.description: The workspace this line belongs to. Required over MCP; the VS Code tool defaults to its own window.

languageModelTools.name: worker
languageModelTools.modelDescription:
Control async OpenCode workers. Pick `action`:
- start: run one self-contained packet (profile, dispatchTurnId, baseRevision, objective, allowedFiles, acceptance, expected, command; optional model, thinking, track). Returns a handle at once.
- submit: same packet plus workerId, queued on a warm worker (reuses its session, ~4x cheaper).
- list: live workers with knowledge, nextInputTokens, warmForSeconds; check before start.
- fanout: ONLY when you explicitly want parallel copies of one warm worker: workerId (an IDLE warm worker holding the shared context) + packets (2..8, same fields as start; model/thinking must match the warm worker or be omitted). Forks its session once per packet, each a new worker on the same model so the cache is reused. Max 8 workers run at once (PARALLEL_CAP).
- status | wait | cancel | resume | logs: by runId. status adds the report (evidence) once the run is terminal. wait blocks at most 240s (timeoutSeconds), then STILL_RUNNING: end your turn. logs: facts only (limit).
Replies are bounded JSON facts, never transcripts.

profile.description: Worker mode: build, code, test, explore, research, verify, gradle, rca, review, quality, perf, authoring, devx.

model.description: provider/model; must be allowed by the mode. Omit for the mode default.

thinking.description: Reasoning variant; must be allowed by the mode.

dispatchTurnId.description: The orchestrator turn this work is attributed to.

baseRevision.description: Explicit commit, tag, or remote ref.

allowedFiles.description: Files the worker may change; empty means read-only.

command.description: One simple verification command run from the repo root, e.g. `rtk npm --prefix tasksync-chat run test:workers`. No cd, &&, |, ; or redirects.

track.description: Your plan's track for this packet, e.g. "A"; the Workers tab shows one lane per track.

model.description: provider/model; must be allowed by the mode. Omit for the mode default.

thinking.description: Reasoning variant; must be allowed by the mode.

allowedFiles.description: Files the worker may change; empty means read-only.

command.description: One simple verification command run from the repo root, e.g. `rtk npm --prefix tasksync-chat run test:workers`. No cd, &&, |, ; or redirects.

track.description: Your plan's track for this packet, e.g. "A"; the Workers tab shows one lane per track.

languageModelTools.name: askaway_webex
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Webex actions: spaces lists recent spaces; read reads a room (mine:true learns your writing style); thread reads roomId+parentId; search filters recent room messages by query; people finds email/displayName; send posts to roomId or toPersonEmail with optional parentId. Output is bounded to 50 messages and 1000 characters each, with truncation/pagination flags. Sends require approval showing recipient and full text; when not Here they return a draft. Disabled unless Webex is configured. Never supply tokens or secrets.

askaway.validator.live.description: The reviewer turns this on when the validator is ready. Only while Away in this workspace, requested low-risk reversible sourced answers may act for the reviewer.

askaway.cloud.enabled.description: Allow explicitly requested cloud tasks on the active PR. Never launches tasks automatically.

askaway.cloud.pollMinutes.description: Minutes between cloud PR status polls; polling never launches new tasks.

askaway.cloud.agentLogins.description: Authenticated cloud agent report logins. Model claims remain self-reported.

askaway.cloud.digestTime.description: Local time for the once-daily changed cloud-task digest through the configured remote channel. Never launches cloud tasks.

askaway.localModel.baseUrl.description: Base URL of a local OpenAI-compatible model server (LM Studio, Ollama, etc.) used for memory summarization and embeddings. No Copilot credits are consumed by these calls.

askaway.localModel.summarizationModel.description: Local chat model used to distill sub-agent output into durable memory notes. If empty or unavailable, AskAway stores a trimmed raw capture instead (no summarization).

askaway.localModel.embeddingModel.description: Local embedding model used to vectorize memory notes for semantic search. If empty or unavailable, memory_search falls back to keyword matching.

askaway.mcpEnabled.description: Always start MCP server on activation. Enable this if you use AskAway with external IDEs like Kiro, Cursor, or Antigravity.

askaway.mcpAutoStartIfClients.description: Automatically start MCP server if external client configurations are detected (Kiro, Cursor, Antigravity).

askaway.userMemoryDirectory.description: User markdown memory source directory, read only during one-time migration.

askaway.repoMemoryDirectory.description: Repository markdown memory source directory, read only during one-time migration.

askaway.mcpPort.description: Fixed port for the MCP server. Set to 0 for dynamic port assignment.

askaway.autoRegisterMcp.description: Automatically register MCP server with Kiro and other supported clients.

askaway.autopilot.description: Enable Autopilot to automatically respond to ask_user prompts without waiting for your input, using a customizable prompt you can configure in Settings. Queued prompts always take priority over Autopilot responses.

askaway.autopilotText.default: You are temporarily in autonomous mode and must now make your own decision. If another question arises, be sure to ask it, as autonomous mode is temporary.
askaway.autopilotText.description: Text returned when Autopilot is enabled. The agent receives this as an automatic response.

askaway.autopilotPrompts.description: Array of prompts that cycle in order during Autopilot (1→2→3→1...). Each prompt is sent sequentially with human-like delay. When empty, falls back to autopilotText.

askaway.responseTimeout.description: Auto-respond to pending tool calls if user doesn't respond within this time. When Autopilot is enabled, the Autopilot text is sent. When disabled, a session termination message is sent.

askaway.sessionWarningHours.description: Show a one-time warning after this many hours (0..8) in the same session. Set to 0 to disable session warning.

askaway.maxConsecutiveAutoResponses.description: Maximum consecutive auto-responses (from timeout) before terminating session. Prevents infinite loops.

askaway.turnBudgetAiu.description: Soft per-turn credit budget in AIU. When the agent calls the turn_budget tool and this is exceeded, it is advised to wrap up. 0 = disabled (no soft limit).

askaway.subagentModel.markdownDescription: Experimental. When set, a PreToolUse hook rewrites the `model` argument of Copilot's built-in `runSubagent` tool so sub-agents run on this (cheaper) model — e.g. `Claude Haiku 4.5 (copilot)`. Must be an exact model string your plan supports and that can run agentic sub-agents, else sub-agents may fail. Leave empty to disable. Requires a window reload to install the hook.

askaway.humanLikeDelay.description: Add random human-like delays before auto-responses (Autopilot, Queue, Timeout). Simulates natural reading and typing time.

askaway.humanLikeDelayMin.description: Minimum delay in seconds before auto-responses when human-like delay is enabled.

askaway.humanLikeDelayMax.description: Maximum delay in seconds before auto-responses when human-like delay is enabled.

askaway.sendWithCtrlEnter.description: Use Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) to send messages instead of Enter.

askaway.notificationSound.description: Play a notification sound when the AI triggers the ask_user tool.

askaway.interactiveApproval.description: Show interactive approval and choice buttons for Yes/No questions and multiple choice options.

askaway.webex.enabled.description: Enable Webex integration to post questions and receive answers via a Webex space.

askaway.webex.tokenFilePath.description: Path to a JSON file containing a Webex access_token (e.g. ~/PycharmProjects/AET/session_data/webex_token.json).

askaway.webex.accessToken.description: Webex personal access token (used only if tokenFilePath is not set).

askaway.webex.roomId.description: Webex Room/Space ID where AskAway posts questions. Get this from the Webex API (GET /rooms).

askaway.webex.notifyOnTurnEnd.description: Post the agent's 'Response Handoff' section to the Webex room when a turn ends.

askaway.webex.clientId.description: Webex Integration Client ID for OAuth token refresh. Get this from developer.webex.com/my-apps.

askaway.webex.clientSecret.description: Webex Integration Client Secret for OAuth token refresh.

askaway.webex.refreshToken.description: Webex OAuth Refresh Token. Used to auto-renew access tokens when they expire. Obtained via the OAuth authorization flow.

askaway.telegram.enabled.description: Enable Telegram integration to post questions and receive answers via a Telegram bot.

askaway.telegram.botToken.description: Telegram Bot Token. Create a bot via @BotFather on Telegram to get this.

askaway.telegram.chatId.description: Telegram Chat ID where AskAway posts questions. Use the 'AskAway: Get Telegram Chat ID' command to auto-detect.

askaway.telegram.notifyOnTurnEnd.description: Post the agent's 'Response Handoff' section to the Telegram chat when a turn ends.

askaway.telegram.liveCommentary.description: Mirror the Commentary tab into one live Telegram message per turn, edited as lines arrive and marked complete when the turn ends.

askaway.workers.keepWarm.description: While the main chat is active, send one minimal ping to an idle worker whose prompt cache is about to expire, so it stays warm for reuse. A ping is a real request (cost shown in worker spend); it stops at 300K context or after 4 unused pings.

askaway.telegram.retryIntervalSeconds.description: Telegram reply polling retry interval in seconds after initial quick retries. Increase for lower API traffic, decrease for faster pickup of late replies.

askaway.telegram.idlePauseMinutes.description: Pause Telegram polling when Copilot is idle for this many minutes. Set to 0 to disable idle pause so replies can still be picked up later.

askaway.reusablePrompts.description: Saved reusable prompts accessible via /slash commands.

name.description: Short name for the prompt (used with /slash command)
